svg.text: Verified directly from services/*.py — the waterfall is NOT uniform across endpoints (see red annotations)

g.text: 2. NeonDB — PlaceCache table (Postgres via Prisma-managed conn)
_db_get(cacheKey) — same cacheKey string as unique index; expiresAt = now + DB_TTL_DAYS (30 days)
check_only=True and BOTH Redis+DB miss → return None (short-circuits, never calls Google)
only reached if check_only=False AND both cache tiers missed
_db_set() → PlaceCache row saved FIRST, then _cache_set() → Redis populated SECOND
Confirmed: matches the standard 3-tier waterfall exactly
Redis → PlaceCache (Postgres) → Google Places API, in that order, for BOTH /api/places and /api/food
(food uses the same function with a food-category query variant — same cache path, same key scheme)
check_only short-circuits cleanly BEFORE the external call, once both cache tiers report a miss
same 30-day-style TTL convention as Places cache
query filtered on city, check_in_date, check_out_date
composite unique: (hotel_id, city, check_in_date, check_out_date) — enforced via ON CONFLICT upsert
check_only=True and DB miss → return None here (skips SerpAPI)
only reached if check_only=False AND both cache tiers missed
Hotel table upsert FIRST (ON CONFLICT composite key), then Redis _cache_set() SECOND
Confirmed: also matches the standard 3-tier waterfall
Redis → Hotel table (Postgres) → SerpAPI, same order/shape as Places/Food
check_only correctly short-circuits after DB miss, before the paid SerpAPI call
same "DB write before Redis write" ordering on cache population
GET /api/transport — NOT a uniform waterfall: 4 independent per-mode paths, dispatched concurrently by rank_transport()
⚠ Confirmed: NO Redis layer exists anywhere in the transport path — only Places/Food/Hotels use Redis
last resort; result saved back to Train table
hard `return None` — NO cache check at all
Bus DB-cache path is DEAD CODE
fetch_redbus_api() exists but is NOT in the
no Redis, no live DB cache read in practice
a pure heuristic / math result synthesizer
no DB read, no Redis: fabricates plausible timings
effectively ignored — strategy never reads it,
No Redis. No Postgres table lookup.
no write-back — nothing to cache to
rank_transport() always awaits cab search regardless
composite unique: (flight_no, origin, dest, dep_time, arr_time)
on DB miss → returns empty; no write-back
despite the filename, nothing here is "live"
queries Flight table first; None only if truly empty
check_only query parameter — api.py: check_only: bool = Query(False), threaded into rank_transport() and each mode fn
Purpose (frontend polling flow): let the UI ask "is there already-cached data?" without triggering slow/costly live calls.
If rank_transport() returns None for a mode → api.py returns {'{'} "status": "cache_miss" {'}'} for that mode (line ~319–320).
Only FLIGHT implements true "check DB cache, return early" semantics. TRAIN is a no-op stub (always cache_miss). BUS ignores the flag
(its only active strategy always synthesizes data). CAB never receives/respects check_only — it always executes the live call.
Cache miss → fall through to next tier
Cache miss at final tier → external API call (last resort)
Blue = Places/Food (Google Places), Green = Hotels (SerpAPI), Orange = Transport (mixed — no single pattern)
Only /api/places, /api/food, /api/hotels follow the "Redis → Postgres cache table → external API" 3-tier waterfall.
/api/transport does NOT — it is 4 structurally different paths (GTFS+legacy DB+live API / dead-code+heuristic / zero-cache / DB-only-no-live) unified only by a shared dispatcher.
api.py — route handlers dispatch to engines/ranking_engine.py: rank_places(), rank_food(), rank_hotels(), rank_transport()
services/live_hotels_api.py — search_live_hotels(): Redis key f"hotels_{'{'}CITY{'}'}_{'{'}check_in{'}'}_{'{'}check_out{'}'}", Hotel table upsert ON CONFLICT
services/live_trains_api.py — search_live_trains(): GTFS tables → Train table DOW cache → RailRadar; check_only returns None unconditionally
services/live_bus_api.py — search_live_buses(): active strategy list = [scrape_redbus_mobile] only; fetch_redbus_api() is unused dead code
services/osrm_cab_api.py — search_live_cabs(): no cache reads/writes of any kind; always calls OSRM + Open-Meteo
services/live_flights_api.py — _search_live_flights_impl(): Flight table only; "External API Fallback removed as per user request"
engines/ranking_engine.py — rank_transport() comment confirms cabs "never check_only... always return results"; dispatches all 4 modes concurrently
